fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: Project name (naming prefix)
fields.help: Prefix used for every resource: <project_name>-<env>-<role>.

fields.name: region
fields.label: AWS Region
fields.help: AWS region code (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1, ...).

fields.name: aws_access_key
fields.label: AWS Access Key ID
fields.help: IAM user access key ID.

fields.name: aws_secret_key
fields.label: AWS Secret Access Key
fields.help: IAM user secret access key. Store in the encrypted secret store.

fields.name: auth_method
fields.label: VM login method
fields.help: 'ssh_key' creates an aws_key_pair from your public key. 'password' uses cloud-init to create a Linux user with password login.

fields.name: ssh_public_key
fields.label: SSH public key
fields.help: ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa public key. Registered as an aws_key_pair and attached to every instance.

fields.name: admin_username
fields.label: Admin username
fields.help: Linux user created on every instance via cloud-init, with sudo NOPASSWD.

fields.name: admin_password
fields.label: Admin password
fields.help: Password for the admin user. Injected via cloud-init user_data.

fields.name: vpc_cidr
fields.label: VPC CIDR
fields.help: IPv4 CIDR block for the VPC.

fields.name: subnet_cidr
fields.label: Subnet CIDR
fields.help: Public subnet CIDR (must sit inside the VPC CIDR).

fields.name: admin_cidrs
fields.label: Admin CIDRs (SSH port 22)
fields.help: JSON array of source CIDRs allowed on port 22, e.g. ["203.0.113.10/32"]. Restrict in production.

fields.name: enable_web_ingress
fields.label: Allow web ingress (ports 80/443)
fields.help: When enabled, opens 80 and 443 on the security group.

fields.name: web_cidrs
fields.label: Web CIDRs (ports 80/443)
fields.help: Source CIDRs allowed on 80/443. Ignored if web ingress is disabled.

fields.name: custom_ingress_rules
fields.label: Custom ingress rules (any port / CIDR)
fields.help: JSON array of extra ingress rules on the main security group. Each entry is an object with description, protocol (tcp/udp/icmp/-1), from_port, to_port, cidr_blocks. Example: [{"description":"App API","protocol":"tcp","from_port":8080,"to_port":8080,"cidr_blocks":["10.0.0.0/8"]}]

fields.name: ami_id
fields.label: AMI ID (optional)
fields.help: Leave empty to auto-select the latest Canonical Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64 AMI in the region.

fields.name: instance_type
fields.label: Default instance type
fields.help: EC2 instance type (t3.micro, t3.small, m5.large, c6i.xlarge, ...).

fields.name: app_vm_count
fields.label: App VM count
fields.help: Number of generic app VMs. Leave 0 if you only want the Platform pool.

fields.name: platform_roles
fields.label: Platform roles (rename / add / remove, set count + instance type per role)
fields.help: Edit role names inline, set VM count, and optionally override the instance type per role.

fields.name: enable_alb
fields.label: Provision Application Load Balancer
fields.help: Creates an ALB across two subnets in different AZs, a target group and an HTTP listener. App-pool instances are auto-registered.

fields.name: alb_target_port
fields.label: Backend target port
fields.help: Port that App instances listen on. The ALB forwards HTTP traffic to this port.

fields.name: alb_health_check_path
fields.label: Health-check path
fields.help: HTTP path used by the target group to verify instance health.

fields.name: alb_certificate_arn
fields.label: ACM certificate ARN (optional)
fields.help: When set, the ALB also exposes an HTTPS listener on 443 using this ACM certificate.

fields.name: subnet_cidr_b
fields.label: Second subnet CIDR (different AZ)
fields.help: A second subnet is required by the ALB (and by RDS). Created automatically in a different AZ.

fields.name: enable_rds
fields.label: Provision Amazon RDS
fields.help: Creates a managed RDS instance in a private DB subnet group. Reachable from the App security group on the engine port.

fields.name: rds_engine_version
fields.label: Engine version (optional)
fields.help: Empty = AWS default. Examples: '16.4' (postgres), '8.0' (mysql).

fields.name: rds_instance_class
fields.label: Instance class
fields.help: db.t3.micro, db.t3.small, db.m5.large, ...

fields.name: rds_password
fields.label: Master password
fields.help: Stored encrypted. Required when RDS is enabled.

fields.name: rds_publicly_accessible
fields.label: Publicly accessible
fields.help: Leave off unless you need to reach the DB from outside the VPC.

fields.name: rds_skip_final_snapshot
fields.label: Skip final snapshot on destroy
fields.help: Turn off for production so RDS keeps a snapshot when the stack is destroyed.

fields.name: enable_s3
fields.label: Provision S3 bucket
fields.help: Creates a bucket for backups, logs, assets and state files.

fields.name: s3_bucket_name
fields.label: Bucket name (globally unique)
fields.help: S3 bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts.

fields.name: s3_block_public_access
fields.label: Block all public access
fields.help: Recommended. Turn off only if you intentionally serve public content from the bucket.

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: Project name (naming prefix)
fields.help: Prefix for every resource: <project_name>-<env>-<role>.

fields.name: region
fields.label: AWS Region
fields.help: AWS region code (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1, ...).

fields.name: aws_access_key
fields.label: AWS Access Key ID
fields.help: IAM user access key ID with EKS + EC2 + IAM permissions.

fields.name: aws_secret_key
fields.label: AWS Secret Access Key
fields.help: IAM user secret access key. Stored encrypted per stack.

fields.name: kubernetes_version
fields.label: Kubernetes version
fields.help: EKS control-plane version (e.g. 1.30, 1.31, 1.32). Must be a version currently supported by AWS EKS in your region.

fields.name: create_iam_roles
fields.label: Create IAM roles
fields.help: Turn off if your AWS user cannot create IAM roles. You must then provide existing EKS role ARNs.

fields.name: existing_cluster_role_arn
fields.label: Existing EKS cluster role ARN
fields.help: Role trusted by eks.amazonaws.com with AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController.

fields.name: existing_node_role_arn
fields.label: Existing EKS node role ARN
fields.help: Role trusted by ec2.amazonaws.com with AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, and AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly.

fields.name: public_subnet_cidrs
fields.label: Public subnet CIDRs (one per AZ, min 2)
fields.help: JSON array of at least 2 CIDRs. EKS requires subnets in different AZs.

fields.name: availability_zones
fields.label: Availability zones (optional)
fields.help: JSON array like ["us-east-1a","us-east-1b"]. Leave empty to auto-pick the first N AZs.

fields.name: endpoint_public_access
fields.label: Public API endpoint
fields.help: Expose the EKS control plane publicly. Turn off for private clusters.

fields.name: endpoint_private_access
fields.label: Private API endpoint
fields.help: Expose the EKS control plane inside the VPC.

fields.name: public_access_cidrs
fields.label: Public API CIDRs
fields.help: CIDRs allowed to reach the public EKS API. Restrict in production.

fields.name: primary_instance_type
fields.label: Instance type
fields.help: EC2 instance type (t3.medium, m5.large, c6i.xlarge, ...).

fields.name: extra_node_groups
fields.label: Extra node groups (JSON map)
fields.help: Map of group_name -> object. Keys: instance_type, disk_size_gb, capacity_type, ami_type, desired_size, enable_autoscaling, min_size, max_size, labels. Example: {"gpu": {"instance_type": "g4dn.xlarge", "desired_size": 1, "labels": {"gpu": "true"}}}

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: Project name (naming prefix)
fields.help: Prefix used for every resource: <project_name>-<env>-<role>.

fields.name: gcp_project_id
fields.label: GCP Project ID
fields.help: The Google Cloud project id (e.g. 'my-org-prod-1234').

fields.name: region
fields.label: GCP Region
fields.help: GCP region (us-central1, europe-west1, asia-southeast1, ...).

fields.name: zone
fields.label: GCP Zone
fields.help: Zone inside the region (e.g. us-central1-a). VMs are created in this zone.

fields.name: gcp_credentials_json
fields.label: Service Account JSON key
fields.help: Paste the full JSON key file for a service account with Compute Admin + Network Admin. Stored encrypted.

fields.name: auth_method
fields.label: VM login method
fields.help: 'ssh_key' injects your public key via instance metadata. 'password' uses cloud-init to create a Linux user with password login.

fields.name: ssh_public_key
fields.label: SSH public key
fields.help: ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa public key. Attached to every instance via ssh-keys metadata.

fields.name: admin_username
fields.label: Admin username
fields.help: Linux user for SSH (created via cloud-init when auth_method='password', or used as the metadata key user).

fields.name: admin_password
fields.label: Admin password
fields.help: Password for the admin user. Injected via cloud-init user_data.

fields.name: subnet_cidr
fields.label: Subnet CIDR
fields.help: Primary CIDR range for the auto-created subnet in the selected region.

fields.name: admin_cidrs
fields.label: Admin CIDRs (SSH port 22)
fields.help: JSON array of source CIDRs allowed on port 22. Restrict in production.

fields.name: enable_web_ingress
fields.label: Allow web ingress (ports 80/443)
fields.help: Opens 80/443 on the firewall when enabled.

fields.name: web_cidrs
fields.label: Web CIDRs (ports 80/443)
fields.help: Source CIDRs allowed on 80/443.

fields.name: custom_ingress_rules
fields.label: Custom ingress rules (any port / CIDR)
fields.help: JSON array of extra firewall rules. Each entry is an object with description, protocol (tcp/udp/icmp), ports (list of strings — single "8080" or range "30000-32767", omit for icmp), and source_ranges. Example: [{"description":"App API","protocol":"tcp","ports":["8080"],"source_ranges":["10.0.0.0/8"]}]

fields.name: image
fields.label: Boot image
fields.help: GCE image in '<project>/<family-or-image>' form. Default = Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.

fields.name: machine_type
fields.label: Default machine type
fields.help: GCE machine type (e2-small, e2-medium, n2-standard-2, c3-standard-4, ...).

fields.name: disk_size_gb
fields.label: Boot disk size (GB)
fields.help: Boot persistent disk size in gibibytes.

fields.name: app_vm_count
fields.label: App VM count
fields.help: Number of generic app VMs. Leave 0 if you only want the Platform pool.

fields.name: platform_roles
fields.label: Platform roles (rename / add / remove, set count + machine type per role)
fields.help: Edit role names inline, set VM count, and optionally override the machine type per role.

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: Project name (naming prefix)
fields.help: Prefix for every resource: <project_name>-<env>-<role>.

fields.name: gcp_project_id
fields.label: GCP Project ID
fields.help: The Google Cloud project id (e.g. 'my-org-prod-1234').

fields.name: node_service_account_email
fields.label: GKE node service account email
fields.help: Optional. Empty = use the client_email from the JSON key for GKE nodes. Grant IAM roles to that service account email, not only to your human Google user.

fields.name: manage_node_service_account_act_as_binding
fields.label: Auto-grant node service account access
fields.help: OpenSible will add Service Account User on the selected node service account. The JSON key service account needs Service Account Admin, because OpenTofu runs as the JSON key identity, not your Cloud Shell user.

fields.name: region
fields.label: GCP Region
fields.help: Region for the VPC and (for regional clusters) the control plane.

fields.name: zone
fields.label: GCP Zone (zonal clusters only)
fields.help: Zone for a zonal cluster (e.g. us-central1-a). Ignored for regional clusters.

fields.name: cluster_type
fields.label: Cluster type
fields.help: Regional clusters span 3 zones (HA control plane). Zonal clusters are cheaper but single-zone.

fields.name: gcp_credentials_json
fields.label: Service Account JSON key
fields.help: Paste the full JSON key. Its client_email is the identity OpenSible uses, so grant roles/container.admin, roles/compute.networkAdmin, and if auto-grant is enabled roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin to this service account email.

fields.name: kubernetes_version
fields.label: Kubernetes version
fields.help: Empty = GKE picks the default for the selected release channel (recommended).

fields.name: release_channel
fields.label: Release channel
fields.help: STABLE lags behind but is safest. REGULAR is the GKE default.

fields.name: subnet_cidr
fields.label: Subnet CIDR (nodes)
fields.help: Primary CIDR for node IPs.

fields.name: pods_cidr
fields.label: Pods secondary CIDR
fields.help: Secondary range for Pod IPs (VPC-native / alias IP). Must not overlap the node subnet.

fields.name: services_cidr
fields.label: Services secondary CIDR
fields.help: Secondary range for ClusterIP Services.

fields.name: master_authorized_cidrs
fields.label: Master authorized networks
fields.help: JSON array of CIDRs allowed to reach the GKE control plane. Restrict in production.

fields.name: enable_private_nodes
fields.label: Private nodes (Cloud NAT for egress)
fields.help: When ON, nodes have no public IP and a Cloud NAT is created for outbound traffic.

fields.name: primary_machine_type
fields.label: Machine type
fields.help: e2-standard-2, n2-standard-4, c3-standard-4, ...

fields.name: primary_node_count
fields.label: Node count per location (fixed size)
fields.help: Regional clusters multiply this by 3 (one per zone).

fields.name: primary_preemptible
fields.label: Preemptible / Spot nodes
fields.help: Cheaper but Google may reclaim the VM at any time. Not for stateful workloads.

fields.name: extra_node_pools
fields.label: Extra node pools (JSON map)
fields.help: Map of pool_name -> object. Keys: machine_type, disk_size_gb, disk_type, node_count, enable_autoscaling, min_nodes, max_nodes, preemptible, labels. Example: {"gpu": {"machine_type": "n1-standard-4", "node_count": 1, "labels": {"gpu": "true"}}}

fields.name: location

fields.help: Hetzner location code (nbg1, fsn1, hel1, ash, hil, sin).

fields.name: hcloud_token

fields.help: Create in Hetzner Cloud Console → Project → Security → API Tokens (Read & Write).

fields.name: auth_method

fields.name: ssh_public_key

fields.help: ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa public key. Uploaded to the Hetzner project and injected into every server.

fields.name: admin_username

fields.help: Linux user created on every VM via cloud-init, with sudo NOPASSWD.

fields.name: admin_password
fields.label: Admin password
fields.help: Password for the admin user. Stored encrypted; injected via cloud-init user_data. Password SSH login is enabled on the VM.

fields.name: network_cidr
fields.label: Network CIDR
fields.help: Private network range for the Hetzner project.

fields.name: app_subnet_cidr

fields.help: Subnet inside the network CIDR where app + platform VMs attach.

fields.name: admin_cidrs

fields.help: JSON array of source CIDRs allowed on port 22, e.g. ["203.0.113.10/32"]. Use your office/VPN IP in production.

fields.name: enable_web_ingress

fields.name: web_cidrs

fields.help: Source CIDRs allowed on 80/443. Ignored if web ingress is disabled.

fields.name: custom_ingress_rules

fields.help: JSON array of extra inbound rules. Each entry is an object with description, protocol (tcp/udp/icmp), port ("22" or range "30000-32767", omit for icmp), and source_ips. Example: [{"description":"App API","protocol":"tcp","port":"8080","source_ips":["10.0.0.0/8"]}]

fields.name: image
fields.label: Default image
fields.help: Hetzner image name (ubuntu-24.04, debian-12, ...).

fields.name: server_type
fields.label: Default server type
fields.help: Hetzner server type (cx22, cpx11, cax11, cpx31, ...).

fields.name: app_vm_count
fields.label: App VM count
fields.help: Number of generic app VMs to create. Leave 0 if you only want the Platform pool.

fields.name: platform_roles
fields.label: Platform roles (rename / add / remove, set count + server type per role)
fields.help: Edit role names inline, set VM count, and optionally override the server type per role.

fields.name: load_balancer_type
fields.label: Load balancer type
fields.help: lb11 / lb21 / lb31 — Hetzner LB size.

fields.name: os_project_name

fields.name: os_domain_name

fields.name: image

fields.help: Used as the prefix for every hostname: <project_name>-<env>-<role>.

fields.name: region
fields.label: Region / location
fields.help: IDCloudHost datacenter — Jakarta or Singapore.

fields.name: api_token
fields.label: IDCloudHost API token
fields.help: Create the token in the IDCloudHost dashboard (Account → API). Stored encrypted per stack.

fields.name: server_plan
fields.label: Server plan
fields.help: IDCloudHost vision plan size (CPU / RAM).

fields.name: os_image
fields.label: OS image
fields.help: OS template name (ubuntu-24.04, debian-12, ...).

fields.name: ssh_public_key

fields.help: ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa public key injected into the server.

fields.name: app_vm_count
fields.label: App VM count
fields.help: Number of app VPS instances to provision.

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: Project name (naming prefix)
fields.help: Used as prefix and label on managed resources.

fields.name: api_token
fields.label: Cloudflare API Token
fields.help: Create in Cloudflare Dashboard → My Profile → API Tokens. Needs Zone:Edit, DNS:Edit, Workers/R2/Access scopes as required.

fields.name: account_id
fields.label: Cloudflare Account ID
fields.help: Right-hand sidebar of any zone overview page in the Cloudflare dashboard.

fields.name: zone_name
fields.label: Zone (domain)
fields.help: Root domain — e.g. example.com. Used for records, worker routes, and Access apps.

fields.name: create_zone
fields.label: Create the zone in Cloudflare
fields.help: OFF (default): use an existing zone (data source). ON: creates it (you must change registrar nameservers).

fields.name: dns_records
fields.label: DNS records (JSON array)
fields.help: Each record: {"name","type","content","ttl","proxied"}. Use "@" for the zone apex. ttl 1 = automatic.

fields.name: r2_buckets
fields.label: R2 buckets (JSON array)
fields.help: Each bucket: {"name","location"}. location optional (e.g. "wnam", "enam", "weur").

fields.name: workers
fields.label: Worker scripts (JSON array)
fields.help: Each: {"name","content","module":false}. content is the JS source string.

fields.name: worker_routes
fields.label: Worker routes (JSON array)
fields.help: Each: {"pattern":"example.com/api/*","script_name":"my-worker"}.

fields.name: access_apps
fields.label: Access applications (JSON array)
fields.help: Each app: {"name","domain","session_duration":"24h","allowed_emails":["user@corp"]}. Emails list creates an allow-policy.

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: ByteDC Project Name
fields.help: Resource space name from ByteDC console (Service List > Resource Space). Used for the HCS provider.

fields.name: name_prefix
fields.label: Stack Project Name (Naming Prefix)
fields.help: Prefix used for VM/VPC/ELB names: <prefix>-<env>-<role>. Falls back to ByteDC Project Name when empty.

fields.name: region
fields.label: Region
fields.help: ByteDC region ID from the console, e.g. cn-north-1.

fields.name: vpc_name
fields.label: VPC name (optional)
fields.help: Custom VPC display name. Leave blank to use the default <prefix>-<env>-vpc.

fields.name: admin_cidr
fields.label: Admin CIDR (SSH/admin UIs)
fields.help: Your office/public CIDR allowed to reach port 2222 + admin UIs. Example: 203.0.113.10/32.

fields.name: use_existing_network
fields.label: Reuse an existing VPC / subnets
fields.help: Off by default — the stack creates its own VPC, subnets and SGs. Turn on only when you want this stack to plug into an existing network so multiple stacks can reach each other.

fields.name: existing_vpc_id
fields.label: Existing VPC ID
fields.help: Required when reuse is on. When set, VPC creation is skipped. You MUST also fill all three subnet IDs below (Public, App, Data) — otherwise new subnets are created inside the existing VPC and may collide with your CIDRs.

fields.name: existing_public_subnet_id
fields.label: Existing Public Subnet ID
fields.help: Required when reuse is on.

fields.name: existing_app_subnet_id
fields.label: Existing App Subnet ID
fields.help: Required when reuse is on.

fields.name: existing_data_subnet_id
fields.label: Existing Data Subnet ID
fields.help: Required when reuse is on.

fields.name: existing_public_ipv4_subnet_id
fields.label: Existing Public IPv4 Subnet ID (ELB only)
fields.help: Only required if Enable ELB is on. The neutron IPv4 subnet ID of the public subnet (different from the VPC subnet ID).

fields.name: existing_app_ipv4_subnet_id
fields.label: Existing App IPv4 Subnet ID (ELB only)

fields.name: existing_data_ipv4_subnet_id
fields.label: Existing Data IPv4 Subnet ID (ELB only)

fields.name: existing_app_sg_id
fields.label: Existing App SG ID (optional)
fields.help: Reuse the previous stack's app-sg so you don't get duplicate-name conflicts. Leave blank to create a fresh SG.

fields.name: image_id
fields.label: ByteDC IMS image ID
fields.help: e.g. Ubuntu 22.04 image UUID. Used as the default for the Platform pool.

fields.name: flavor_id
fields.label: Default flavor
fields.help: Fallback flavor for Platform pool roles that don't set their own.

fields.name: platform_roles
fields.label: Platform roles (rename / add / remove, set count + subnet + flavor per role)
fields.help: Edit role names inline, set VM count, pick subnet (data/app), and optionally override the flavor per role. Leave flavor blank to use the default.

fields.name: enable_nat
fields.label: Enable NAT / outbound egress
fields.help: For a new VPC, this creates a NAT gateway. For an existing VPC, leave this off unless you also provide an Existing NAT Gateway ID or explicitly create a new NAT in that VPC.

fields.name: domain_base
fields.label: Domain base
fields.help: Base DNS domain for the private zone, e.g. internal.example.com.

fields.name: use_existing_nat
fields.label: Reuse / manage an existing NAT gateway
fields.help: Off by default. Turn on only when you want to plug into an existing NAT gateway (or intentionally create another NAT inside a reused VPC).

fields.name: existing_nat_gateway_id
fields.label: Existing NAT Gateway ID (optional)
fields.help: Use this when the selected existing VPC already has a NAT gateway. The stack will not create a duplicate NAT gateway.

fields.name: create_nat_in_existing_vpc
fields.label: Create new NAT inside existing VPC
fields.help: Advanced: only turn on when you intentionally want this stack to create another NAT gateway in a reused VPC.

fields.name: manage_existing_nat_snat_rules
fields.label: Manage SNAT rules on existing NAT
fields.help: Usually off. Turn on only if you provide NAT EIP ID and want this stack to add SNAT rules to an existing NAT gateway.

fields.name: nat_floating_ip_id
fields.label: NAT EIP ID (optional)
fields.help: Existing EIP ID for NAT. Required only when managing SNAT rules on an existing NAT gateway.

fields.name: ecs_admin_pass
fields.label: ECS Admin Password
fields.help: Default root/admin password seeded into every provisioned VM. Stored encrypted.

fields.name: ssh_port
fields.label: Custom SSH Port
fields.help: Port opened on the app/data security groups from the Admin CIDR. Golden image ships on 2222.

fields.name: extra_users
fields.label: Extra Linux Users
fields.help:
List of additional users seeded on every VM. Example:
[{"name": "alice", "password": "Str0ng!Pass", "sudo": true, "ssh_key": "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."}]

fields.name: ingress_rules
fields.label: Extra Security Group Ingress Rules
fields.help:
List of extra inbound rules applied to the app SG. Example:
[{"protocol": "tcp", "port": 8080, "cidr": "10.0.0.0/8", "sg": "app", "description": "internal api"}]
sg: "app" | "data" (default app).

fields.name: env
fields.label: Environment
fields.help: Short env tag — dev / sit / prod.

fields.name: project_name
fields.label: Project name (naming prefix)
fields.help: Used as label prefix on every Kubernetes object OpenSible creates.

fields.name: auth_method
fields.label: Cluster auth method
fields.help: 'kubeconfig' pastes the full YAML (recommended, works with EKS/GKE/AKS/k3s). 'token' uses cluster endpoint + CA cert + bearer token instead.

fields.name: kubeconfig
fields.label: Kubeconfig YAML
fields.help: Paste the full kubeconfig file (~/.kube/config). Stored encrypted, written to <stack>/kubeconfig.yaml (chmod 600) only at execution time.

fields.name: cluster_endpoint
fields.label: API server URL
fields.help: https://<cluster-endpoint>:6443

fields.name: cluster_ca_cert
fields.label: Cluster CA certificate (base64)
fields.help: Base64-encoded CA cert (the value from `kubectl config view --raw` under `certificate-authority-data`).

fields.name: cluster_token
fields.label: Service-account bearer token
fields.help: Bearer token for a ServiceAccount with sufficient RBAC (cluster-admin for the sample workloads).

fields.name: namespace_name
fields.label: Namespace name
fields.help: Kubernetes namespace to deploy into.

fields.name: create_namespace
fields.label: Create namespace if missing
fields.help: OFF: assume it exists (data lookup). ON: OpenSible creates it.

fields.name: workloads
fields.label: Workloads (JSON array)
fields.help: Each workload: {"name","image","replicas","port","env":{K:V}}. Creates one Deployment + ClusterIP Service per entry.

fields.name: enable_ingress
fields.label: Enable Ingress
fields.help: Creates a single Ingress in front of one of the workloads' services.

fields.name: ingress_class
fields.label: Ingress class
fields.help: IngressClass name (e.g. 'nginx', 'traefik'). Requires a controller installed on the cluster.

fields.name: ingress_host
fields.label: Ingress host
fields.help: FQDN, e.g. app.example.com. Must resolve to your ingress controller's external IP.

fields.name: ingress_target_workload
fields.label: Target workload name
fields.help: Name of the workload above whose Service should receive the ingress traffic.

fields.name: ingress_target_port
fields.label: Target service port
fields.help: Port exposed by the workload's Service.

fields.name: ingress_tls
fields.label: Enable TLS (uses cert-manager 'letsencrypt-prod' issuer)
fields.help: Adds cert-manager annotations so certs are issued automatically. Install cert-manager below if not already present.

fields.name: install_ingress_nginx
fields.label: Install ingress-nginx
fields.help: Deploys the ingress-nginx controller (helm chart, namespace 'ingress-nginx').

fields.name: install_cert_manager
fields.label: Install cert-manager
fields.help: Deploys cert-manager into the 'cert-manager' namespace (CRDs included).

fields.name: install_metrics_server
fields.label: Install metrics-server
fields.help: Deploys metrics-server into 'kube-system' (needed for HPA / `kubectl top`).
